newsitem.title: GREECE: Greece extends $100 million credit to Yugoslavia.
newsitem.headline: Greece extends $100 million credit to Yugoslavia.

text.p: Greece will extend a $100 million credit to Yugoslavia for infrastructure projects and open a consulate in the southern town of Nis, Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos said on Tuesday.

"We expressed interest in construction projects such as the Belgrade-Skopje road. For such projects a line of credit worth $100 million will be opened," he told reporters after meeting his visiting Yugoslav counterpart Milan Milutinovic.
He said Athens would open a consulate in the southern Yugoslav town of Nis to accomodate visa-seeking travellers to Greece and help Belgrade rejoin international diplomacy.

Milutinovic, who asked for the trouble-free entry of Yugoslavs to Greece, said his country was grateful to Athens for its support in getting Belgrade back into the international community after its isolation during the Bosnian war.
"We appreciate Greece's dynamic support in helping us return to the international organisations from which we were unjustly expelled," Milutinovic told reporters.

Greece has backed the Orthodox Christian Serb-led Yugoslav government throughout the Balkan conflict, often angering its western allies who shunned Belgrade for its role in the fighting in neighbouring Croatia and Bosnia.

The four-year Bosnian war ended with the 1995 Dayton peace accord but delays in impementing it have stalled the peace process. Milutinovic said Belgrade was committed to impementing the Dayton agreement.
